Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12299 of 2022
Applicant :- Ramesh Chandra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhilasha Singh,Ashutosh Yadav,Shyam Lal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the
material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 393 of
2022, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Sirsaganj, District Firozabad.

Facts in brief are that vehicle bearing No. UP82 T4052 was seized by the authorities regarding which a forged release order was filed by the applicant for the purposes of getting the vehicle released and order was said to be passed by the Mines Assistant order dated 28.06.2022.

During the course of verification it was found that neither the application for release of the vehicle was filed nor such release order was issued by the office of the authority even the entry was not found in the dispatch register.

There was mention that compounding fee/ penalty amount in Rs. 39,340 were deposited in the State Bank of India through challan number GE00074 on 28.06.2022 but on Ramesh Chandra vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13524892/
1 verification it was also found to be forged and no such amount was deposited through challan in the bank.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The verification was confirmed by the Treasury Officer, Firozabad, as a result, present F.I.R.
was lodged against the applicant and investigation is still going on.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has committed no offence.
He paid Rs. 50,000 to the learned counsel who handed over him, the release order which was produced by him.
The preparation of forged release order cannot be said to be made by the present applicant but it might have been made by the counsel to whom he handed over the money for this purpose.

It is also submitted that in a similar case the Session Judge granted anticipatory bail to other accused person Jitendra Kumar in anticipatory bail application 7118 of 2022 by order dated 02.09.2022 and the matter in the present case is on similar footing, therefore, requested for anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant also.
Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record and without making any comment on the merit of the case, it appears that F.I.R. was lodged after getting the papers verified by the authorities, therefore, at this stage there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant and in which circumstances learned In-charge Session Judge passed the order in anticipatory bail application No. 7118 of 2022 on 02.09.2022 he may know well himself.
Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is, hereby, rejected.

Order Date :- 21.2.2023 Suraj Srivastav  Ramesh Chandra vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13524892/
